node.label: Gu Jiegang
node.date_label: Letters on the layering of ancient historical traditions (1923) · Gushibian volume1 and autobiographical preface (1926) · Edition of Cui Dongbi/Cui Shu’s writings (1936) · The Chinese Nation Is One (1939) · Index of the Shangshu (1962)
node.description: A Chinese historian, philologist and folklorist who examined the accumulated layers of ancient historical traditions rather than treating transmitted narratives as transparent records. Richter describes both his 1923 critique of unitary origins and his recovery of earlier Chinese source criticism. The relation between that scepticism and his 1939 national-unity thesis remains contested: Jenco reads an open political community, whereas Kim and Zheng stress homogenizing limits. Dirlik reports contemporary Marxist objections to restricting criticism to documents; Lu questions aspects of Gu’s source chronology.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Stratification correspondence (1923); editor, Gushibian (from 1926); autobiographical preface (1926; Arthur W.Hummel’s English translation 1931); edition of Cui Dongbi/Cui Shu (1936); The Chinese Nation Is One (1939); Shangshu index (1962).
node.scope_note: Read on 2026-10-24: Richter’s complete 1982 obituary and the opening/references of her separate China Quarterly article; PKU biography; Lu’s Chinese/English abstracts; Jenco’s publisher abstract; Kim’s English abstract; Zheng’s Gu discussion; Dirlik’s selected epilogue passages. Gu’s original works remain unread. Chinese intellectual and philological traditions are not treated as mere imports of European methods. The 1926 series start is supported by Richter’s references; her obituary’s 1927 date is retained here as a source discrepancy, not silently harmonized. Jenco’s and Kim’s divergent interpretations remain attributed.

incident_edges.evidence_note: Richter describes Gu’s text criticism and recovery of earlier Chinese critics; Lu’s abstract analyzes the distinction between original records and later transmission. The target is the cross-tradition field Critical historical scholarship, not a claim of dependence on Ranke.

incident_edges.relationship: Ancient unity questioned and the Chinese nation reformulated: a contested trajectory (1923–1939)
incident_edges.evidence_note: Richter describes Gu’s early challenge to a unitary ancient origin. Zheng reads the 1939 unity thesis critically; Jenco’s abstract emphasizes a politically open, plural community, while Kim’s emphasizes retreat toward homogenization. These disagreements remain explicit; no single retrospective verdict is adopted.

incident_edges.relationship: Li Ji and Liang Yuantong object that antiquity-doubting must move beyond documents to their social conditions, as Dirlik reports
incident_edges.evidence_note: Dirlik’s epilogue, p. 265, reports these Marxist historians’ methodological criticism. Their original texts are unread. The named objection is routed through Marxist historiography, not equated with a consensus of that whole field.
